items.followUp: What is the purpose of the decision symbol in a flowchart?

rubric.why: The terminal symbol marks the beginning and ending points of a flowchart.
rubric.description: Identifies the start and end points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it shows the start and end of a flowchart.

rubric.why: The symbol helps show where the flowchart begins and where it terminates.
rubric.description: Explains its role in showing where the flowchart begins and terminates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it indicates where the flowchart begins or ends.

modelAnswer: The terminal symbol shows the beginning and end of a flowchart.
It is used to mark the start and stop points of the process.

items.followUp: What is meant by a jump in an algorithm?

rubric.why: GOTO is the notation used to direct the algorithm to another step.
rubric.description: Identifies GOTO as a transfer or jump to another step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying GOTO as a jump or transfer notation.

rubric.why: The notation directs execution to a named or numbered location in the algorithm.
rubric.description: States that execution continues at a specified step, label, or line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it transfers control to a specified location.

modelAnswer: GOTO is used in an algorithm to transfer control to another step.
It directs execution to a specified step, label, or line.

items.followUp: What is the main purpose of tags in a markup language?

rubric.why: A markup language uses notations or tags to identify parts of a document.
rubric.description: Identifies a markup language as a language that uses markup or tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning markup, tags, or a suitable example such as HTML.

rubric.why: Markup tags describe the structure or presentation of document content.
rubric.description: States that markup describes a document’s structure or presentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating what the tags describe or control.

modelAnswer: A markup language uses tags to mark and identify elements in a document.
These tags describe the structure or presentation of the document; HTML is an example.

items.followUp: Give two examples of attributes used in HTML tags.

rubric.why: Attributes provide additional information or properties for an HTML element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that attributes provide extra information or properties for an element.
Award 1 mark for giving at least two valid attribute names.

modelAnswer: HTML attributes provide extra information or properties for an element.
They are written in the opening tag as name-value pairs, for example href="page.html" and src="image.jpg".

items.followUp: What digits are used in the binary number system, and what is its base?

rubric.why: Binary uses only the digits 0 and 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that binary uses 0 and 1.

rubric.description: States the base of the binary system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its base as 2.

modelAnswer: The binary number system is a number system with base 2.
It uses only two digits: 0 and 1.

items.followUp: Give one example of a non-volatile storage device.

rubric.why: Volatile memory requires power to retain its contents.
rubric.description: Describes volatile memory’s dependence on power or loss of data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that volatile memory loses its contents when power is turned off.

rubric.why: Non-volatile memory retains data without power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that non-volatile memory keeps data when power is turned off.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory loses its stored data when the power is turned off.
Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is turned off.

items.followUp: Write the truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.why: The table must include all four possible pairs of binary inputs.
rubric.description: Shows the four input combinations for the OR operator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for listing all four input combinations.

rubric.why: OR gives 1 when at least one input is 1, and gives 0 only when both inputs are 0.
rubric.description: Gives the correct OR output for every input pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly matching all four input pairs with their outputs.

rubric.why: Counterfeiting involves making or distributing something that falsely imitates a genuine product.
rubric.description: Identifies the product or item as fake or imitative.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that counterfeiting involves a fake or imitation product.

rubric.why: The fake item is passed off as a genuine or original product.
rubric.description: States that the fake is represented as genuine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the imitation is presented as genuine or original.

modelAnswer: Counterfeiting is making or distributing a fake imitation of a genuine product, such as software.
The imitation is passed off as original or authentic.
